fossil
The papersThe code

Zinc binding from sequence, dug back up.

The authors' predictor is gone, so we rebuilt it from the paper and ran it again on the paper's own evaluation sets, with new sequence profiles. Of 38 results, 2 came back exactly, 6 agree, 14 partly agree, 5 cannot be told apart, 6 differ and 5 were not attempted.

Our predictor calls fewer human proteins: in the sample it recovers 81 of the 100 proteins both methods called and 10 of the 50 only the SPCH-SVM called, so the estimate is 2,010 (SE 101) against 2,833. Refitting the Platt constants to our own CV margins raises it to 2,223 (SE 94); the rest is open.

Python package spsvm and its tutorialAgrees

The paper's main claim holds: the gated predictor beats the local one in both tests, on cysteines and on histidines, and overall by more than the error bars. The AURPCs, the proteome count and the single probabilities do not come back; the likely causes, still open, are our 2010 profiles in place of the lost 2005 ones and the Platt constants tuned on those.

What came back

The zinc sites
From today's PDB files the multiple-site-type counts of Table 1 come back exactly, once only side-chain donors of six residue types count.
Fig. 1
The correlation curves overlay the published ones, read as C and H pairs counted by the residues between them.
The main claim
Gated beats local in leave-one-out and in CV, on C and on H. The leave-one-out AUCs are 0.893 and 0.913 (paper 0.895 and 0.914).
D and E
The leave-one-out AUCs of aspartate and glutamate come back as printed: 0.74 and 0.70.
Fig. 8's protein
A 2018 crystal structure (5ZLQ) binds zinc with exactly the four cysteines the paper predicted, the one at 0.67 included. Our predictor ranks the same four highest.
The paper's own arithmetic
Its proteome counts (2,833 predicted, 965 of 3,207 not confirmed, 591 new) follow from its Additional file 3; our own scan predicts about 2,010.

What stayed buried

  • The authors' C++ predictor and its 2005 profiles
  • Nine of the 305 zinc chains, absent from Additional file 1
  • The reliability levels behind Fig. 7, in a paywalled supplement
  • How the printed AURPCs were computed: they sit 0.033 below the paper's own curves

The paper's main claim holds: the gated predictor beats the local one in both tests, on cysteines and on histidines, and overall by more than the error bars. The AURPCs, the proteome count and the single probabilities do not come back; the likely causes, still open, are our 2010 profiles in place of the lost 2005 ones and the Platt constants tuned on those.
